claim: A classifier built from the 1000 gene-expression measurements separates the two groups of subjects with a balanced accuracy (mean of sensitivity and specificity) of at least 0.60 on new subjects.

data_keys.meaning: expression level of each gene in the blood sample of each subject
True when the subject belongs to the second group

claim: Within crustacean species, claw length rises with abdomen length after accounting for total body length: across species, the mean of the within-species coefficients of abdomen length in a linear regression of claw length on abdomen length and body length is at least 0.15.

data_keys.meaning: Abdomen length of each measured individual, in mm.
Length of the larger claw of each measured individual, in mm.
Total body length of each measured individual, in mm.

sizes: species = 15, individuals = 40 per species; abdomen_length, claw_length and body_length each have shape (15, 40).

claim: Across subjects, mean resting heart rate and mean salivary cortisol (each subject's mean over the recording days) are positively correlated: the Pearson correlation between the two subject means is positive, and a test of that correlation gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: resting heart rate in beats per minute of each subject on each recording day
morning salivary cortisol concentration of each subject on each recording day

sizes: subjects = 16; days = 10 (heart_rate and cortisol: 16 x 10 = 160 values each)

claim: Across critically ill patients, whole-body oxygen uptake measured by expired-gas analysis is positively correlated with systemic oxygen delivery (cardiac output times arterial oxygen content): the Pearson correlation is at least 0.3.

data_keys.meaning: Cardiac output of each patient by thermodilution, in L/min.
Arterial blood oxygen content of each patient, in mL O2 per dL.
Mixed venous blood oxygen content of each patient, in mL O2 per dL.
Whole-body oxygen uptake of each patient from expired-gas analysis, in mL/min.

sizes: patients = 60; cardiac_output, arterial_o2_content, venous_o2_content and o2_uptake_expired each have shape (60,).

claim: In each participant's own region of visual cortex that responds more to faces than to houses, the response to faces exceeds the response to bodies: across the 12 participants the mean difference (faces minus bodies) of the response in that region is at least 0.3 percent signal change, and a one-sided paired t test across participants is significant at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: response to face images (percent signal change) of each visual-cortex voxel in each scanning run of each participant
response to body images (percent signal change), same layout
response to house images (percent signal change), same layout

claim: In the voxels of this participant's visual cortex whose responses follow stimulus contrast, the response rises with contrast: the regression slope of the voxel-averaged response (percent signal change) on stimulus contrast across the 240 trials is at least 0.2 percent signal change per unit of contrast, with a one-sided p value below 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: response of each visual-cortex voxel on each trial, in percent signal change
stimulus contrast shown on each trial, in units where full contrast equals 1

claim: A classifier that uses three genes distinguishes tumour from normal colon tissue with an accuracy of at least 0.70 on new tissue samples.

data_keys.meaning: expression level of each gene in each colon tissue sample
True when the tissue sample is tumour tissue

claim: The task engages region A more than region B: the task-evoked signal change (task minus rest) is larger in region A than in region B, with the mean across subjects of the within-subject difference of the two signal changes positive, and a paired t test of that difference gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: mean signal in region A of each subject during task blocks (percent signal change units)
mean signal in region A of each subject during rest blocks
mean signal in region B of each subject during task blocks
mean signal in region B of each subject during rest blocks

sizes: subjects = 24 (each of the four keys: 24 values)

claim: Across trials of an estimation task, the estimates of the three observers are positively associated after accounting for the true value of the quantity: the mean, over the three pairs of observers, of the partial correlation between the two observers' estimates given the true value is at least 0.2.

data_keys.meaning: Actual value of the quantity presented on each trial, in arbitrary units.
Estimate of the quantity made by each observer on each trial, in the same units as true_value.

sizes: trials = 200, observers = 3; true_value has shape (200,); estimates has shape (200, 3).

claim: Giving the compound in the drinking water reduces body-weight gain: the mean weight gain of animals receiving the compound is lower than that of controls, and a Welch two-sample t test of the difference between the two group means gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: body-weight gain in grams over the study of each animal housed in each cage
whether the drinking water supplied to the cage contained the compound

sizes: cages = 40; animals = 2 (weight_gain: 40 x 2 = 80 values; treated: 40 values)

claim: Among patients whose symptom score at the screening visit was at least 60, at least 40% improve by 10 points or more between the start of the programme and the 6-month follow-up (score at the start minus score at 6 months of at least 10); the claim is that the proportion of such patients is at least 0.40.

data_keys.meaning: symptom score of each patient at the screening visit (higher is worse)
symptom score of each patient at the start of the programme
symptom score of each patient at the 6-month follow-up

claim: Across adult skeletons, femur length and tibia length are positively associated after accounting for humerus length: the partial correlation between femur length and tibia length, given humerus length, is at least 0.3.

data_keys.meaning: Maximum length of the femur of each skeleton, in mm.
Maximum length of the tibia of each skeleton, in mm.
Maximum length of the humerus of each skeleton, in mm.

sizes: skeletons = 1000; femur_length, tibia_length and humerus_length each have shape (1000,).

claim: In adult mice, liver weight is positively related to kidney weight after accounting for body mass: the coefficient of kidney weight in a linear regression of liver weight on kidney weight and body mass is at least 0.25 (g of liver weight per g of kidney weight).

data_keys.meaning: Wet liver weight of each mouse, in g.
Combined wet weight of both kidneys of each mouse, in g.
Body mass of each mouse, in g.

sizes: mice = 150; liver_weight, kidney_weight and body_mass each have shape (150,).

claim: Across the advanced economies in the post-war period, average real GDP growth in country-years with a public debt ratio above 90 percent of GDP is at least 2 percentage points lower than average real GDP growth in country-years with a debt ratio of 90 percent or below.

data_keys.meaning: real GDP growth rate in percent of each country in each year
public debt as a percentage of GDP of each country in each year

claim: Scores on the task and on the symptom scale are more strongly related in group A than in group B: the Pearson correlation between task score and symptom score is higher in group A than in group B, and a Fisher z test of the difference between the two correlations gives two-sided p < 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: score of each participant on the experimental task
score of each participant on the symptom questionnaire
whether the participant belongs to group A (true) or group B (false)

sizes: participants = 40 (each of the three keys: 40 values)
